source_text:
τὸ δὲ εἰς τὸν Μωϋσῆν ἐβαπτίσαντο ἐν τῇ νεφέλῃ καὶ
ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ, σημαίνει τοῦτο ὅτι καθάπερ ἐκεῖνοι τούτων τυχόντες ὑπέσχοντο τοῖς
Μωϋσαικοῖς νόμοις βιοῦν, οὕτω καὶ ἡμεῖς ἐν τῷ βαπτίσματι τὸ τῆς υἱοθεσίας
κομιζόμενοι πνεῦμα, συνθήκας καὶ ὁμολογίας τιθέμεθα τοῦ κατὰ τὰς Χριστοῦ
λοιπὸν ζῆν ἐντολάς.
{ 1 Kor 12,28} τὰ ἐνεργήματα δηλονότι τῶν δυνάμεων.
{ 1 Kor 13,2} Νῦν πίστιν οὐ τὴν τῶν πιστῶν ἔφη, τὴν κοινὴν καὶ καθολικήν,
ἀλλὰ τὸ χάρισμα τὸ τῆς πίστεως· ἦν γάρ τι χαρίσματος εἶδος ὁμωνύμως οὕτω τῇ
πίστει λεγόμενον, ὅθεν ἐπὶ φανερώσει πνευματικῆς μετουσίας ἐχορηγεῖτο πολλοῖς
ἐν τῷ τότε τῶν εὐσεβῶν.
thought_title: Baptism into Moses as a type of Christian baptism
orientation: Gennadius is explaining Paul's statement that Israel was baptized into Moses in the cloud and sea, drawing out its meaning for Christian baptism.
pass_a_gloss: But the 'into Moses they were baptized in the cloud and in the sea' means this: that just as those men, having obtained these things, promised to live by the Mosaic laws, so also we, in baptism receiving the Spirit of adoption, make covenants and confessions to live henceforth according to the commandments of Christ. The workings, clearly, of the powers. Now he did not speak of the faith of the faithful, the common and universal faith, but the spiritual gift of faith; for there was a kind of spiritual gift called by the same name as faith, whence it was supplied to many for the manifestation of spiritual participation in the time of the pious of that day.

choices.term: τὸ δὲ εἰς τὸν Μωϋσῆν ἐβαπτίσαντο
choices.why: Keeps the quoted Pauline phrase as the subject of the sentence, preserving the source's grammatical structure where the article makes the quotation a substantive.
Renders the demonstrative and explanatory clause literally, preserving the forward-pointing force of τοῦτο.
Keeps both nouns distinct and the verb 'make' literal, reflecting the legal and declarative acts of baptismal commitment.
Preserves the participial clause and the genitive 'of adoption' as modifying 'Spirit', matching the source's word order and theological precision.

choices.english: the workings, clearly, of the powers
choices.why: Keeps the parenthetical δηλονότι as 'clearly' and the genitive 'of the powers' after the noun, preserving the explanatory aside's tone.
rejected: the activities of powers, that is

choices.english: called by the same name as faith
choices.why: Renders ὁμωνύμως literally as 'by the same name', preserving the point that the spiritual gift shares the name 'faith' with common faith.

bible_refs.note: εἰς τὸν Μωϋσῆν ἐβαπτίσαντο ἐν τῇ νεφέλῃ καὶ ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ
Νῦν πίστιν οὐ τὴν τῶν πιστῶν ἔφη

pass_b_english: The phrase “they were baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea” (1 Corinthians 10:2) means this: just as those people, having obtained these things, promised to live by the Mosaic laws, so we too, receiving the Spirit of adoption in baptism, make covenants and confessions to live from then on according to Christ’s commandments.
On 1 Corinthians 12:28, “the workings, clearly, of the powers.”

Now when he says “faith,” he does not mean the faith of believers, the common and universal faith, but the spiritual gift of faith. For there was a kind of spiritual gift called by the same name as faith, which was supplied to many among the pious of that time for the manifestation of spiritual participation.

last_rejected.why: Glossary mandates 'spiritual gift' for χάρισμα, but first instance uses 'gift' alone.
last_rejected.fix: For there was a kind of spiritual gift called by the same name as faith
last_rejected.ruling: Source has χάρισμα alone; 'spiritual gift' adds πνευματικοῦ not in text. No glossary break; translator clarified meaning.

problems.why: Four different renderings for related pneumatological concepts may seem distinct.
problems.fix: Use consistent terminology for the Holy Spirit's work.

problems.quote: The workings, clearly, of the powers (1 Corinthians 12:28).
problems.why: No transition from baptism discussion to 1 Cor 12:28; reader cannot tell who is speaking or why.
problems.fix: Add a section break or transitional sentence introducing the new verse.

edits.old: The workings, clearly, of the powers (1 Corinthians 12:28).
edits.new: On 1 Corinthians 12:28, “the workings, clearly, of the powers.”

fixed: The glossary issue about 'Spirit of adoption' is not a real problem: the English already uses the standard phrase 'Spirit of adoption' consistently with the glossary entry for υἱοθεσία as 'adoption,' and the source itself uses the same phrase.
